[SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:386] `readStoredLineageSessionId` reuses the stored session id of any non-complete lineage config. [SOURCE: .skilled/hooks/session-relaunch/lib/killer.cjs:796] Because the lineages are detached, a runtime SIGTERM does not reach their groups. That comment says Codex delivers no background-task completions as prompts. **NEW: a cheaper fix mechanism already exists in-repo.** The goal plugin records `session.status` per session and suppresses its continuation while a session is `busy` or `retry`. [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/opencode-goal.js:3623] [SOURCE: .opencode/plugins/opencode-goal.js:3038] The report's fix ("skip the arm while a tracked child is busy") could reuse that event. [INFERENCE: based on opencode-goal.js:3623-3626 and session-relaunch.js:335-341]

**NEW: a second smallest fix for fan-out.** The runner already keeps per-lineage liveness with pids: a `lineageProcessLiveness` map, and pid-carrying liveness records in the pool. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:3525] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-pool.cjs:176] If the `started` ledger event carried the lineage pid, `detectOrphanedLineages` could skip labels whose pid answers `process.kill(pid, 0)`. That would make the re-run safe even when the nudge-step fix (report change 2) is not followed. Whether `started` records already carry a pid is UNCONFIRMED. [INFERENCE: based on fanout-pool.cjs:176-196 and :284-305]

**RESOLVED UNCONFIRMED ITEM: `markOrphanedLineages` does NOT check pid liveness.** It is defined in `fanout-pool.cjs`, not `fanout-run.cjs`. It calls `detectOrphanedLineages`, which builds its list purely from the ledger: a label with a `started` event and no later `completed`, `failed` or `orphan_requeued` counts as orphaned. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-pool.cjs:284] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-pool.cjs:290] For each one it appends `orphan_requeued` with no process check. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-pool.cjs:307] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-pool.cjs:314] A lineage that is still running is therefore requeued on a re-run.

**STILL INFERRED (orphan claim).** No run was observed, so the orphan claim stays an inference, but the code evidence makes it stronger. A `&` worker leaves its tool shell. The killer's single-pid SIGTERM reaches only the runtime. So nothing in the hop path signals the worker, and it keeps running after the runtime exits. [INFERENCE: based on killer.cjs:796 and session-relaunch.cjs:277-281] To confirm: the process table after a hop that left a `sleep`-style `&` child running.

**STILL UNCONFIRMED: can a child be alive when the parent arms?** No repository code answers it. The relaunch plugin tracks no child status, so a live child would not block the arm. Whether OpenCode's `task` tool can return, and the parent go idle, while a child session still runs is OpenCode runtime behaviour. The missing evidence is OpenCode's task-tool source or an event trace that shows `session.idle` for the parent before the child's own idle. Iteration 2 can try `command opencode --help` for a background-task option. [INFERENCE: based on session-relaunch.js:158-164 and :418-437]

keyFindings.text: **NARROWED, still not observed: an OpenCode child can run past its parent's block.** The installed SDK's v2 client has a `background` call documented as "Detach any synchronous subagents currently blocking the session and continue them in the background." [SOURCE: .opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/v2/gen/sdk.gen.js:284] Its route is `/experimental/session/{sessionID}/background` [SOURCE: .opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/v2/gen/types.gen.d.ts:6710], and a config field `backgroundSubagents: boolean` exists. [SOURCE: .opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/v2/gen/types.gen.d.ts:1747] So OpenCode supports subagents that keep running after the parent is unblocked, and the parent can then reach `session.idle`. That `session.idle` fires for the parent while a backgrounded child is `busy` is inferred, not traced. `SessionStatus` carries `idle`, `retry` and `busy` [SOURCE: .opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/gen/types.gen.d.ts:396], and `session.idle` carries only `sessionID` [SOURCE: .opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/gen/types.gen.d.ts:413], so the plugin must track child status itself, which supports iteration 1's finding 8. Missing evidence: an event trace on 2.2.7 with a backgrounded subagent.

keyFindings.text: **Crons and wakeups end with the session, RESOLVED to CONFIRMED (was UNCONFIRMED).** The official page says: "Tasks are session-scoped." and "Tasks only fire while Claude Code is running and idle. Closing the terminal or letting the session exit stops them firing." It also says `--resume` or `--continue` restores `CronCreate` tasks, but "A self-paced `/loop` isn't restored". [SOURCE: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks] A hop never resumes, because the wrapper denies `claude:-c`, `--continue`, `-r` and `--resume` on replay. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:575] So every `CronCreate` task and every `ScheduleWakeup` wakeup the sender held is gone in the receiver. Claude's help has no schedule, cron or wakeup flag; the grep matched only resume and continue lines. On disk, `~/.claude` has no `todos`, `tasks`, scheduled or cron directory, and this checkout has no `.claude/scheduled_tasks.json`. The page names that file as the store only "With feature-flag fetching off".
sources: `command <binary> --help` for claude, pi, opencode, codex, cursor-agent, devin

keyFindings.text: **Pi mode flags, CONFIRMED for the code, REFUTED in one label.** `--approve`, `--build` and `--plan` are no-value options [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:545] [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:546] that are not record-backed [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/skilled-loop:594], so they replay from launch only. `--approve` is not a mode flag: Pi's help reads `--approve, -a Trust project-local files for this run`. `--plan` and `--build` come from an extension: `Extensions can register additional flags (e.g., --plan from plan-mode extension).`, `--plan Start in Plan mode`, `--build Start in Build mode`. Whether the relaunch extension can read the plan-mode extension's live state is UNCONFIRMED. The missing evidence is the plan-mode extension's source or Pi's extension API for reading another extension's mode.
